mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change falls below -2% (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines for four consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 3% for two months signals a dual tightening of monetary and cost pressures, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 3% for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 15% signals a collapse in residential construction activity, which negatively impacts construction and material sector earnings and drags S&P 500 returns lower over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by more than 15% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when HOUST declines by more than 15% month-over-month (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two months indicates labor market churning, which can precede earnings downgrades and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both PAYEMS and UNRATE rise over two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below -5% for three months signals reduced household buffer capacity, which dampens consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < -5% annualized for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower when RSAFS is below -5% annualized for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).
